The Assistant Commissioner of Police, V.V.Puram Sub- division Bangalore has submitted charge sheet against the accused for the offences punishable U/s.498-A , 306, 304-B of Indian Penal Code in Channammanakere Achukattu PS. , Crime No.248/2017.
2.

The brief story of the prosecution are as under:
The deceased-Smt.Sugandhi Durga is the daughter of the complainant.
The deceased-Smt.Sugandhi Durga and Deepak.A.G. are the wife and husband.
The marriage of deceased and accused was performed on 22.05.2013.

After marriage, the deceased and accused were residing together within the limits of Channammanakere Channamanakere Achukattu Ps vs Dipak A G on 7 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/154046907/

sentences.text: 1 Achukattu PS.
Due to the marital relationship, the deceased gave birth to a baby girl.

When the accused and deceased were residing together at No.31, 1st Cross, Grape Garden, Thyagarajanagar, Bengaluru, at that time the accused has been harassing the deceased physically and mentally to bring additional dowry.

Again on 07.07.2017 at 9.30 p.m, the accused quarreled with the deceased and abetted her to die and go to her mother's house with her child, due to the continuous torture of accused, the deceased became anguish and on same day i.e. on 07.07.2017 after 9.30 p.m she has committed suicide by hanging herself with saree to the ceiling hook at her matrimonial home and thereby the accused has committed the offenses alleged against him.

3. The concerned police have submitted charge sheet before the jurisdictional 44th ACMM.,
Bangalore.
The learned Magistrate has took cognizance of the offences and committed the case to the Sessions Court by complying Sec.207 of Cr.P.C. by furnishing charge sheet copies to the accused persons.
The same was numbered as SC No.96/2018.
4. The charge was framed against the accused only for the offences punishable U/s.498-A and 304-B of Indian Penal Code.
The accused has pleaded not guilty and claims to be tried.
5. The prosecution has examined thirteen witnesses as PW.1 to 8 and got marked documents at Ex.P1 to P20 and MO.1.
On consent of accused counsel, inquest Mahazar, postmortem report have been marked at EX.P10 and P11.
As such learned PP has gave up the witnesses CW7 to 9, 12, 13, 15 to 19 are given up.
The learned PP has also dropped CW.5, 6 and 11 and gave up witness CW14 in view of evidence of other police official witnesses.
The concerned police failed to produce the witness C.W.5, 6, 11 inspite of issue of witness SS, NBW and proclamation.
As such, the prayer of learned Public Prosecutor rejected and the said witnesses CW5, 6, 11 were dropped.
Thereafter the prosecution side evidence was taken as closed.
6. After completion of prosecution side evidence, this Court has recorded the statement of accused as provided U/s.313 of Cr.P.C.

The accused has denied incriminating evidence present against him,
and not opted to lead defense evidence nor submitted anything to the Court.

The accused has complied Sec.437-A of Cr.P.C.
7. Heard the arguments of both sides and perused the materials on record.

8. The following points that arises for consideration of this court:
1 . W h e t h e r t h e p r o s e c u t i o n p r o v e s t h a t t h e a c c u s e d h u s b a n d o f deceased-Smt.Sugandhi Durga subjected deceased physical and mental harassment for silly reasons and demanded additional dowry from her parental home and thereby the accused has committed the offence punishable under Section 498-A of IPC?

sentences.text: Whether the prosecution proves that the accused being the husband of the deceased- Smt.Sugandhi Durga harassed the deceased physically and mentally and demanded additional dowry from her parental home, due to the ill- treatment and harassment on 07.07.2017 after 9.30 p.m committed suicide by hanging herself and ended her life and thereby the accused has committed the offence punishable u/s 304-B of IPC?
3. What order?

9. This Court findings on the above points are as under:
Point No.1: In the Negative Point No.2: In the Negative Point No.3: As per final order for the following:-
REASONS 10. Points No.1 and 2 : These points are taken up together as they are related to each other and to avoid repetition in the discussion.
Admittedly, the deceased and accused are the wife and husband.
Due to the marital relationship, the deceased has given birth to a baby girl.
The both accused and deceased along with their child residing at No.31, 1st Cross, Grape Garden, Thyagarajanagar, Bengaluru.

It is the allegation that the accused has been harassing the deceased physically and mentally to bring additional dowry and on 07.07.2017 at 9.30 p.m, the accused quarreled with the deceased and abetted her to die and go to his mother's house with the child, due to the continuous torture of accused, she became anguish and on same day after 9.30 p.m she has committed suicide by hanging herself with a saree to the ceiling hook at her marital home and thereby the accused has committed the offenses alleged against him.
11.
The prosecution is required to establish the physical and mental harassment having received by the deceased from the accused.

To prove the said allegations, the prosecution has examined PW1-Mr.Harimurthy, PW2-Ranjini, PW3-Smt.Manjula Devi, PW4-Smt.Hemalatha, who are none other than the father, mother and sisters of the deceased respectively.

The said witness PW1 is being signatory to the complaint has not supported the contents of the complaint though the complaint allegation shows that the accused has been harassing the deceased soon before her death by demanding dowry, but the evidence given before the court by the said witness does not establish any dowry harassment or physical and mental torture given by the accused to the deceased.

So also the mother PW2 and sisters PW3 and PW4 have also did not spoken anything with regard to physical and mental harassment given by the accused to bring additional dowry and due to which deceased has ends her life by hanging herself.
No doubt the said witnesses have given proper evidence with regard to the marriage of accused and deceased.
But the said witnesses have denied giving of ill- treatment by the accused to the deceased.
The complainant PW1 has also not supported the Mahazar and statement alleged to be given before the police.

Since, the evidence of PW1 to 4 goes Channamanakere Achukattu Ps vs Dipak A G on 7 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/154046907/
3 against to the route of the prosecution case, hence, the learned PP has cross-examined the said witnesses.

sentences.text: But unfortunately not able to get any useful evidence in support of this case.
12. Such being the case, the prosecution has examined PW1-Mr.Harimurthy i.e. complainant and PW5-Smt.Shanthi, who are the signatories to the mahazar marked at EXP2 to prove Mahazar contents.
The said pancha witnesses not supported conducting of Mahazar marked at EX.P2 by stating that the police have not conducted mahazar in their presence and they do not know the contents of the mahazar.
As such, learned PP has treated the panchas and other family members of the deceased i.e., PW1 to PW5 as hostile with the permission of court and cross-examined.
The learned PP has failed to elicit any useful evidence to believe due to the physical and mental harassment given by the accused, the deceased has ended her life.
Hence , the evidence of the family members and panchas not worthful to the case of prosecution to establish guilt against the accused.

13. The evidence of PW6-Mr.S.P.Kumarasway shows that on 08.07.2017 at 11.30 a.m the C.W.1/P.W.1 came to his police station and gave complaint, he received the complaint and registered UDR.20/2017 under 174 Cr.PC, and registered FIR and sent to the concerned Executive Magistrate.

The prosecution has got marked UDR.copy as Ex.P.12 and got marked FIR as Ex.P.13 and conducted panchanama alongwith pancha witnesses CW.10 and 11 and complainant i.e. C.W.1 and got marked Mahazar at Ex.P.2.
At the time of conducting Mahazar Ex.P.2, 6 photos have been marked as Ex.P.5, later sent the dead body alongwith C.W.15 with ligature objects to KIMS Hospital Mortuary.

He submitted requisition to the Tahasildar to prepare inquest Mahazar as the deceased has died within 7 years of her marriage and after post mortem handed over the dead body to C.W.1 and recorded statements of CW.10 to 12 and 15.
On 11.07.2017 C.W.16 has produced the P.M.Report alongwith ligature material i.e. light yellow colour golden border saree and P.W.6 has received and brought into the P.F.No.75/2017.

The report marked at Ex.P. 16, ligature material is marked at M.O.1 and recorded statement of C.W.16, on the same day of incident at 4.00 p.m. he received the complaint from C.W.1 as per Ex.P.1 and registered FIR. at Ex.P.17 and later handed over investigation to C.W.21.
14.
The evidence of PW7-Mr.Krishna.T.T. shows that on 12.07.2017 he has carried out further investigation, he appointed C.W.17 to find out the accused and produce before him.
On same day at 10.00 a.m, the accused Deepak was produced before him and gave report.

He has recorded the statements of C.W.1, 5, 7 and 9, later he collected 65B certificate from C.W.12 and on 13.07.2017, he submitted requisition to CMM Court to record the statements of CWs.1 to 4 u/s.164 of Cr.PC and on 30.08.2017 he requested 2nd ACMM for insertion of Section.304B of IPC, later he handed over the further investigation of this case to C.W.22.

15 . The evidence of PW8-Mr.N.R.Mahantha Reddy, the then ACP shows that on 30.08.2017 he received the further investigation from C.W.21 and after verifying the investigation has submitted charge sheet against the accused.
The learned accused counsel has completely denied the evidence given by the police official witnesses PW6 to 8.
It is no doubt, the prosecution has got marked inquest report at EX.P10 and postmortem report at EX.P11 on consent of accused counsel.
The postmortem report issued by the medical officer shows that the death is due to asphyxia as a result of hanging.
It is no doubt the death of deceased-Smt.Sugandhi Durga is due to hanging.

Whether the Channamanakere Achukattu Ps vs Dipak A G on 7 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/154046907/
4 said death was due to the harassment of the accused as alleged against him is not proved by the prosecution, beyond reasonable doubt.

sentences.text: So it is very clear that the prosecution has failed to establish that the accused has been demanded further dowry and harassed the deceased physically and mentally and due to which the deceased has committed suicide.
Hence in view of above reasons, this court has answered point No.1 and 2 in the Negative.
16. Point No.3:

In view of answer of court on points No.1 and 2, this court pass the following:
ORDER U/s.235(1) of Cr.P.C. the accused is hereby acquitted of the offences punishable U/s.498A and 304(B) of Indian Penal Code.
The bail and surety bonds of accused stand cancelled.
MO1 being Light yellow colour border saree being worthless shall be destroyed after appeal period is over.
